brief: A violent equity selloff and vol spike reversed hard this week. NDX dipped below a major trendline then recovered above it, forming one of its biggest upside candles in a while, even though the 200-day MA still sits above spot, so the squeeze is running against an unresolved downtrend. Hedge fund long/short gross leverage posted its largest weekly drop since Covid to 207.5% (26th percentile) with net leverage at five-year lows. Goldman's new Multiple Surprise Ratio shows SPX's move this week was the largest volatility-adjusted surprise in 19 years, meaning options materially underpriced the swings. Tech positioning now implies outright negative earnings growth and large estimate cuts, semis allocations fell back to year lows, and SOX trades at a single-digit two-year forward P/E. The Market Ear's September 23 NVDA-puts/AAPL-calls relative trade has since exploded and is being closed for profit. TS Lombard argues Nvidia's China AI-chip share fell to 34% (Huawei to 28%) as US export curbs accelerate a domestic rival, leaving Nvidia's 75% gross margin exposed to cheaper Chinese compute. JPM shows Asian tech ex-memory valuations reset to long-term mean P/E despite earnings upgrades; the note says the reset is real but questions whether an earnings reset follows.
